structs.name: bdFileID
structs.size_evidence: no Replay size method applies. Replay carries file IDs as a plain 64-bit value everywhere it touches them: bdContentStreaming::_preDownloadByFileID__Atlas_361A5E0@0x142133D70 takes `__int64 fileId` and writes it with bdByteBuffer::writeUInt64; _preDownloadByFileID__Atlas_361A730@0x142133E60 does the same (plus pageNumber/pageSize); DCache_GetFileIDByFilename@0x1412992E0 returns __int64; XPak_IndexToFileID@0x14159ED40 returns unsigned int. No function is named bdFileID, and no function takes or returns a bdFileID by value or pointer.
structs.notes: Game-test holders: (1) dwCSWriteFileTask, +8 m_outFileID (56 bytes). Replay's closest counterpart, dwCSWriteFileComplete@0x1415066B0(storageRequest, outResult), reads storageRequest+8 as a POINTER to a bdRemoteTask (it calls through the object's vtable at +8 and passes it to bdRemoteTask::getErrorCode), reads the controller index at +21, and writes outResult+120. So +8 holds a pointer there, not an inline 56-byte ID; the name match of storageRequest to dwCSWriteFileTask is not proven and is the one soft link. (2) pooledStorageWriteFileInfo +16664, which is itself absent (see that entry). No Replay struct was found that embeds a bdFileID. A 56-byte immediate scan was not run because 0x38 is too common to be a usable marker. Verdict absent rests on the file-ID APIs taking __int64 and the absence of any holder.

structs.name: bdEventLogID
structs.size_evidence: no Replay size method applies. Game-test has no holder that embeds bdEventLogID by value (game_test_parents_holding_it_by_value is empty). Replay's event log object is bdEventLog (bdEventLog_ctor@0x14212DCA0 writes only +0 vtable/taskManager, +8 enabled byte, +12 count, +528 counter), and the record paths pass it as a pointer (DWEventLog::recordEventsMixed@0x140F75A80 -> bdEventLog::recordEventsMixed@0x14212DE00(a1 = bdEventLog *, outTask, events, count, reservedCtx)). No qword ID is stored at +32 of the event log or of its record task.
structs.notes: bdEventLog::recordEventsMixed reads a 4-byte event type at events+36 with a 72-byte element stride (`v13 += 18` DWORDs) and calls bdBufferParams::addSerializable on events+8*(9*i+2). dwRecordEventInternal@0x141504300, dwRecordEventFF@0x141504100 and dwRecordStringEvent@0x141504490 take an event log from DWServicesAccess::GetEventLog and never take an ID object. The Replay event-record object dwRecordEventObject_ctor@0x1420FB1B0 has the same base pair as the game-test bdEventLogID (bdTaskResult, bdSerializable), which is why earlier passes looked at it; it writes a bool at +32, not an 8-byte ID.

structs.name: pooledStorageWriteFileInfo
structs.size_evidence: no Replay allocation, stride or copy of 16760 (0x4178) bytes. Whole-.text scan of 0x140001000-0x142360000 for 4178h / 16760 / 4190h / 41A8h / 418Ch found no allocation or size argument of this struct (the 4190h / 418Ch / 41A8h hits are stack-frame displacements and other structs' strides; see notes). The only holder in game-test is AnalyticsBuffer, which is itself absent. Game-test pooled storage writer is replaced in Replay by per-slot records inside bdPooledStorage.
structs.notes: Replay's pooled upload path keeps its own per-file data inside the bdPooledStorage object (a1 = bdPooledStorage *): bdPooledStorage::_postUploadFile@0x14213CEA0 reads a WORD at a1+11352+1200*slot and a 0x81-byte name at a1+11354+1200*slot (1200-byte slot records, name capped at 0x80 by memchr), and bdPooledStorage::_preUpload@0x14213D390 writes a single name from a1+22434 and an array of 16-byte entries at a1+25680+64*i (2 qwords, 64-byte stride), then a1+23588 count. None of these is a 16760-byte object and none is a pooledStorageWriteFileInfo member. The upload status path OnlineStorage_LogUploadResult@0x140F53320 reads a different task object (+136 name, +216 user id, +1684 result byte), not this struct. The 16760 size was never measured by Replay code; the 16784 builder value is also unsupported.

structs.name: AnalyticsBuffer
structs.size_evidence: no Replay allocation, stride or copy of 16784 (0x4190) bytes. Whole-.text scan for 4190h / 16784 found no allocation or size argument. The 4190h hits are the stack frame of R_RenderFrustumLightsClusterBuffer (locals are draw state, drawCommands, indirectArgs, range, not an analytics buffer); 418Ch is a voice stream stride (VoiceDecode_InitRemoteStream, VoiceEncode_InitStreamTable / ShutdownStreamTable); 41A8h is a batch offset in R_SunShadow_BuildSurfaceLists. None of these reaches an AnalyticsBuffer.
structs.notes: The analytics spawn path in Replay does not use a buffer object. GScr_BBReportSpawnTypes@0x1413D3210 and GScr_BBReportSpawnPlayerDetails@0x1413D3070 read the script arguments and call DLog_RecordEvent_6@0x1413D0300(logChannel, "analytics_spawn_types_raw_data" / "analytics_spawn_player_details_raw_data", ...). DLog_RecordEvent_6 builds a stack-local context (ctx[14] and buffer[512], 4096 bytes) and calls DLog_CreateContext / DLog_BeginEvent / DLog_RecordContext; the channel buffering lives in DLogHookup (GetChannelBufferTimeMilliseconds@0x140E4BEA0). The analytics streamer dvars (online_analytics_streamer_upload_min_delay_ms, upload failure count max) have no reader in the database (A173), which fits an upload loop that is not in this build's buffer form. Game-test parents: none by value. Replay also has no struct that holds pooledStorageWriteFileInfo, so AnalyticsBuffer is not embedded anywhere.

structs.name: GfxWorldTransientDrawCache
structs.size_evidence: no Replay allocation, memset, copy or stride of 233472 (0x39000) or 344064 (0x54000) bytes. Whole-.text scan (0x140001000-0x142360000) for 39000h / 54000h / 233472 / 344064 found no match. Replay sizes its per-zone world transient data differently: Load_GfxWorldTransientZone@0x140D96E90 loads each zone with Load_Stream(..., 0x148) (328 bytes), and the zone holds its own inline drawVerts (+16, 200 bytes) and drawCells (+216, 24 bytes).
structs.notes: Replay's world-draw side holds 1536 pointers at gfxWorld+392 (Mark_GfxWorldDraw@0x140D9D860 walks 0x600 slots with a pointer stride of 8, calling Mark_GfxWorldTransientZoneAsset). Each pointer is a separately allocated GfxWorldTransientZone (328 bytes), so vertex and cell data is per zone, not one inline block. The data for 1536 zones (200 + 24 bytes each) sums to 344064 bytes, which is where the earlier builder value came from, but no single Replay struct of that size exists. Game-test parents: (1) FxMarkSystemWorldCellCache (cache at +0x12008, alongside a 73736-byte transientDrawContext). Replay has no type or name for it (FxMarkSystemWorldCellCache not in the local types; Replay's FX world zone is FxWorldTransientZone, 160 bytes, a different layout), so the parent is absent. (2) GfxBackEndData at game-test +0x17BDC8 (the cache follows transientDrawContext at +0x169DC0). In Replay GfxBackEndData, transientDrawContext is at 0x173240 (73736 bytes), and its contents are pointer arrays of 1536 entries (drawVertsPtr, drawCellsPtrs, gpuLightGrid, dynLightSets, reflectionProbes, decalVolumes), not inline vertex data. The Replay pad after it (_pad185248, 9550776 bytes) was not read byte by byte; no Replay access to a 233472-byte block there was found, and the scan above found no size constant. Replay's refresh table R_ProcessWorldTransientRefreshAddPending@0x14198EED0 uses a 560-byte record over 64 slots and is unrelated to the cache size.
